concept: Compass aggregation preview sampling versus full pipeline execution
summary: Source-anchored research for Compass aggregation preview sampling versus full pipeline execution. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The Compass settings snapshot distinguishes Number of Preview Documents (output documents shown; default 10) from Limit (documents passed to $group, $bucket, and $bucketAuto; default 100,000). The latter is preview-only and is not applied when the pipeline is run. These are separate controls, so raising the displayed-document count does not raise the documented grouping-input cap. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

A firsthand July 8, 2018 walkthrough explicitly using Compass 1.14.5 places its 100,000-document Sample Mode limit before $group, $bucket and $bucketAuto. This independently corroborates historical input-limit placement, without establishing the current interface or default. (low confidence)

An explicitly authored $limit before $group restricts the inputs that contribute to each group; a $limit after $group restricts the number of group documents returned. Removing Compass's preview-only cap by running the pipeline does not remove an explicit $limit written into that pipeline. Diagnose a truncated count by checking both the preview input setting and the authored stage order. (medium confidence)

COMPASS-10104 identifies Compass 1.48.2 and reports different grouped counts between stage previews and VS Code execution. The reporter acknowledges the preview-only 100,000 input limit and requests clearer stage warnings. This is a user report, not proof of incorrect server aggregation. (low confidence)

A September 2022 community-thread reproduction counted 200,000 documents correctly with MongoDB 6.0.1 and a $group/$sum pipeline; the later response explained Compass's configurable 100,000-document Sample Mode limit. This historical example scopes the apparent ceiling to the builder context rather than establishing a universal 100,000-document server aggregation limit. (medium confidence)

The preview input cap can change computed group results, rather than merely hide some output rows. MongoDB documents that lower input limits improve runtime but can omit documents; COMPASS-9826 identifies the number of documents consumed by blocking stages such as $group as a common cause of preview-versus-execution differences. (medium confidence)

Illustrative consequence, derived from the documented input cap and $group semantics: if 200,000 documents would reach {$group:{_id:null,n:{$sum:1}}}, a preview capped at 100,000 group inputs can display a single result with n=100000, whereas executing the same pipeline without that preview cap counts 200,000. One displayed output document does not mean that every intended input document contributed to its value. This is a semantic example, not a test performed in this research. (medium confidence)
